about.title: Modernizing Historical Land Records with Cadastral AI
about.description: ILRDVS is designed to bridge historical paper records (Modi script, archaic Marathi, and revenue formats) with modern digital land registries, ensuring every land parcel is securely geo-referenced and tamper-proof.
about.mission: Our Mission: 100% digital transparency, zero boundary disputes, and instant citizen access to certified 7/12 extracts.
about.vision: A unified cadastral spatial registry powering citizen empowerment and ease of governance.
about.challengeTitle: The Challenge of Archival Land Records
about.challengeP1: For decades, land records—including Records of Rights (RoR), mutation registers, and registered sale deeds—have been maintained on physical paper, making them vulnerable to yellowing, ink bleeding, tear damage, and manual transcription errors.
about.challengeP2: These vulnerabilities can contribute to duplicate or conflicting land records, ownership disputes, lengthy civil litigation, and delays in land verification. ILRDVS addresses these challenges through an end-to-end AI-powered workflow for digitizing, validating, and verifying land records.
about.auditTrailDesc: Every edit and action is cryptographically tracked
about.accuracyDesc: Validated across Marathi, Hindi, and English
about.pillar1Desc: Adaptive thresholding, deskewing, and multilingual neural recognition of cursive and handwritten Devanagari script.
about.pillar2Desc: Heuristic cadastral parsing isolates Survey No, Khasra, Khata, Plot Area, Owner Name, and Mutation references.
about.pillar3Desc: Dual-pane zoomable review interface enabling revenue officers to verify AI predictions before sanctioning.
about.pillar4Desc: Automated generation of official bilingual certificates with digital seal watermarks and instant print capability.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.subtitle: Find immediate answers regarding 7/12 extracts, mutation applications, and AI verification.
faq.q1: How does the AI OCR digitization work?
faq.a1: Our vision models process scanned Marathi and English land records to transcribe survey numbers, khata details, and boundaries for citizen review and Talathi approval.
faq.q2: What should I do if a discrepancy is detected?
faq.a2: You will receive an alert on your Citizen Portal. Simply review the flagged variance and submit your clarification or supporting tax receipt directly to the officer.
faq.a3: Yes. Approved records carry digital government signatures and QR codes compliant with the Information Technology Act.

items.q1: What is Village Form 7/12 (Satbara Extract) and how is it used?
items.a1: Village Form 7/12 (Satbara Extract) is an official register of rights maintained by the state revenue department. Form 7 contains ownership details, survey and Gat numbers, and land tenancy classifications. Form 12 details crops grown, irrigated areas, and potkharaba (uncultivable land). It is the legal title proof required for land sales, bank agricultural loans, and succession claims.
items.q2: How does the AI OCR Pipeline recognize aged, handwritten Marathi records?
items.a2: ILRDVS employs a specialized multi-stage pipeline: (1) OpenCV adaptive binarization, noise removal, and deskewing; (2) EasyOCR deep convolutional neural networks with language models trained on cursive Devanagari script; and (3) Spatial Named Entity Recognition (NER) that automatically categorizes fields into owner names, survey numbers, khata numbers, and plot areas with confidence scoring.
items.q3: How do I verify the authenticity of a land document on this portal?
items.a3: Citizens and legal practitioners can upload any scanned land document or PDF into the Document Registry or Verification Workstation. The system calculates an SHA-256 cryptographic fingerprint, compares extracted attributes with our verified repository, and validates whether the document holds an active Circle Officer sanction seal.
items.q4: What is Village Form 6 Mutation (Ferfar) and what is the clearance SLA?
items.a4: Form 6 Mutation Register (फेरफार नोंदवही) records any legal title alteration—such as sale deed conveyance, inheritance (वारस नोंद), partition, or mortgage release. Under the Right to Services (RTS) Act, uncontested mutations are mandated to be inspected and certified within 15 working days by the local Talathi and Circle Officer.
items.q5: What is the difference between rural 7/12 Satbara and urban Property Cards?
items.a5: Village Form 7/12 applies to revenue villages and agricultural land governed under the Maharashtra Land Revenue Code 1966. Urban Property Cards (नगर भूमापन मिळकत पत्रिका) are maintained by the City Survey Office (CTSO) for non-agricultural plots and municipal areas, referencing City Survey (CTS) numbers and carpet plot dimensions.
items.q6: How does ILRDVS prevent fraudulent double registration and title disputes?
items.a6: Every parcel is indexed by unique geospatial Survey/Khasra/Khata tuples. When a new deed or mutation is ingested, the system executes real-time duplicate similarity checks across active records, immediately flagging any overlapping deed allocations, seller impersonation, or unreleased bank encumbrances.
items.q7: How do I submit a grievance if my land record contains typographical errors?
items.a7: You can register an online grievance through our Citizen Corner or Contact section below. Revenue inspectors review original physical settlement records, correct typographical spelling errors in the Verification Workstation, and issue an updated, certified digital extract with complete audit logging.
